blocks.content: Aspose.Note enables developers to work with Microsoft OneNote files programmatically in Python. Using the `aspose_note_foss` package, you can load, parse, and convert `.one` files without requiring Microsoft Office or OneNote to be installed. This makes it suitable for server-side processing, automation, and integration into note-taking applications.

Key capabilities include converting OneNote documents to PDF, extracting text and images from pages, and iterating over notebook structure elements like sections and pages. The library supports reading and writing `.one` files in both legacy and modern formats, ensuring compatibility across different OneNote versions.

blocks.content: Install Aspose.Note for Python via pip to access its note processing capabilities. The package `aspose_note_foss` provides core functionality for working with note files in Python environments.
After installation, verify the setup by importing the package in a Python session. A successful import confirms the library is ready for use in your note python code workflows.

Aspose.Note enables programmatic handling of Microsoft OneNote files in Python. Developers can load, manipulate, and export `.one` documents using the `aspose_note_foss` package without requiring Microsoft Office or OneNote installed.

import aspose_note_foss

# Load a OneNote document
notebook = aspose_note_foss.Notebook("sample.one")

The Aspose.Note Python API enables developers to programmatically work with Microsoft OneNote files using native Python note syntax. With `aspose_note_foss`, you can load, inspect, and convert `.one` files without requiring Microsoft Office or OneNote to be installed. This makes it ideal for building note-taking apps, automated documentation pipelines, or integration with enterprise systems.

Common use cases include converting OneNote content to PDF (`python note pdf`), extracting text from notes for indexing (`python note taking app`), or generating structured notes from templates (`python note for professional`). The library supports reading page metadata, child elements, and document structure directly in Python note code.

To get started, import the package and instantiate the `Document` class with a path to a `.one` file. From there, access pages and their content through the exposed API surface. All operations are synchronous and return standard Python types where applicable, ensuring compatibility with existing tooling and frameworks.
